### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 19fc8d6f13772b62cafb3b8cc763cccace407c9b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `279a86ca425c51e3df969102edbb2a4e6034e03c` — the merge of head `a1cd9ce8c383bdfe8e3d93875c7c480b4371bbf5` into base `19fc8d6f13772b62cafb3b8cc763cccace407c9b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 279a86ca425c51e3df969102edbb2a4e6034e03c && git checkout 279a86ca425c51e3df969102edbb2a4e6034e03c
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a1cd9ce8c383bdfe8e3d93875c7c480b4371bbf5`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #20305 (body and comments 5859352607 through 5893277767), PR #20660 (body, its 6-file list, the diff of the head against `main` `6bff748bbd`, merge-base `89801cd963`), and the check-runs on the head. Tree readings by `git show` / `git grep` at the head and, in objectui, at `dd3f7e1be356` (the `.objectui-sha` at the head, unchanged from `main` and equal to the pin the `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tag resolves), at `805abe240c` (the first parent of objectui#10767's merge `17b323e5ca`) and at `f8a9d0fb05` (the pin the decline was measured at).

**Accept set — unchanged, right.** No `*.zod.ts` in the file list; the conversion keeps `retiredFromLoadPath: true` and `retiredAfter: '17.4.0'`, so `normalizeStackInput` / `defineStack` / `validate` never run it and an author writing the record form meets the same door refusal as before. The new §5 pins measure that what the rewrite writes on an inline-row node passes each block door at `filter` with zero issues while the unconverted source is refused there (object-map / -tree / -gantt / -calendar / -kanban). `Clause-②: no` is the right reading.

**Public surface — right.** `rendersInlineRows` was module-private (no `export`), and `git grep` at the head finds no reader anywhere, `scripts/adr-anchors/` included. What moves in published data is the registered entry's `summary` string (the inline clause removed), its `fixture` (`after` for the inline map, `expectedNotices` 4 to 5) and the two D3 `description` strings; no export, conversion id, `toMajor`, `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` order or reach set changes. `spec-changes.json` and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` project protocol 17 only and carry none of this text (grep at the head: zero hits), so leaving them unregenerated is right and the generated-artifact gate agrees.

**Stored-row behaviour — right, and correctly declared.** With the `else if (inline)` branch gone, `rewrite` has two arms: `'declined' in mapping` reports the TODO and returns the holder byte-identical; otherwise it emits and writes `mapping.rules`. Every stored-row seam replays retired entries (`conversions/stored.ts:104` passes `includeRetired: true`; `apply.ts:148` skips a retired entry only when that flag is false), so a page whose inline-row block carried a mappable `filter`, `dataSource.filter` or `defaultFilters` is now rewritten on every read and by the pass, where `main` left it byte-identical with a TODO. In `migrateStoredMetadata` (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`): `changed` is true when at least one notice was emitted; a row with no notice and only TODOs is `skipped` and does not flip `storedMigrationClean` (`pending === 0 && failed === 0`); a row with a notice is `pending` in preview and `rewritten` under `apply`; `cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:724` sets exit 1 when the report is not clean. So such a page moves from `skipped` / exit 0 to `pending` / exit 1 until `--apply` — exactly what the changeset says, and the reason the level is more than a wording change.

**Premise — right, read from source at three commits.** At `dd3f7e1be356`, `ValueDataSource.find`'s array arm calls `toFilterNodeSafely(params.$filter)` and matches `lowered.node`; `toFilterNode` (`core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts:1414`) is the sink `ObjectGrid.tsx` lowers through (`:1917`, `:1927`), so "the grid's own sink" holds. At `805abe240c` and at `f8a9d0fb05` the array arm is `matchesASTFilter(r, params.$filter)` directly, whose first branch refuses any node that is not an array — a rule object — so every row is excluded. `17b323e5ca` is an ancestor of the pin, and the `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tag resolves `.objectui-sha` to `dd3f7e1be356`, so the released 17.5.0 already shipped a renderer the decline protected nothing against. At the pin, `ObjectMap`, `ObjectTree`, `ObjectCalendar` and `ObjectGantt` reach `ValueDataSource` (the gantt through `resolveDataSource`, which returns one for `provider: 'value'`), resolve their rows through `resolveRecordSourceConfig`, and hold the filter through `useResolvedFilter(schema.filter)` for the object fetch and the inline path alike; `plugin-map/src/index.tsx` declares `filter: true` on its `ElementDataSourceMapping`, so the binding is composed into that same `filter`. `ObjectKanban` and `ObjectTimeline` take inline items whole and send `$filter` only on the host fetch; the family's only in-memory matcher is `ValueDataSource`, which lowers, so no block type is left where a rule array selects differently from the stored form. The "114 filters on eight rows" count is the dev's live probe (`premise_probe` in 5893209491) and is not reproducible from the tree; the mechanism behind it is verified above, the count is not.

**Author-shown texts, each sentence against the tree and the pin.**

- Conversion docblock. The inline sentence and its `{@link rendersInlineRows}` are gone; the remaining "What is left exactly as stored" list (top-level `$` keys, AST groups, unspelled operators, a `null` value, an array or object comparand in equality position, a door-refused rule) matches `recordFilterToRules` / `astFilterToRules` / `legacyFilterToRuleArray` at the head, and "Such a row" keeps its combinator antecedent. The new Reach paragraph — row source moves no verdict; measured at `dd3f7e1be356`; the four renderers lower through the grid's sink; the same rows as the stored form; a control without the lowering selects none — is true sentence by sentence per the reading above. The pin is cited in the 12-hex spelling the pin-citation gate accepts (green).
- `summary`. The inline clause is removed; what remains ("a filter carrying `$and` / `$or` / `$not` or any part with no lossless rule spelling is left exactly as stored — reported as a TODO, which `os migrate meta --stored` lists") is exact. Its two tracker citations pre-date this PR and are unchanged; `check:doc-authoring` is green on the head.
- TODO `reason`. The template — `On BLOCK, this filter DECLINED. Left as stored, it keeps loading unchanged, but it is not the rule-array form its door declares — rewrite it by hand.` — is byte-identical to `main` for every remaining decline, and the kept §8 pin asserts that an inline node's `$or` reason equals an object-bound block's. Right.
- D3 `18.element-data-source-and-object-block-filter-rule-array`. "None of this depends on where a block's rows come from … is rewritten or left exactly as it would be on a block that queries an object" — true of the conversion (one `rewrite` path, no node-level branch). "because the object-map, object-tree, object-calendar and object-gantt blocks of the objectui version this release pins match a rule array against those rows and select the rows the stored form selected" — true at the pin both the head and the last release name. "A row left as stored keeps loading unchanged" — antecedent repaired, right. The closing "a row whose only finding is such a TODO is reported `skipped`, and the run's exit code does not change for it" matches `protocol.ts`. Form D, no tracker number.
- D3 `18.object-grid-default-filters-rule-array`. The inline-grid clause is removed; the list that remains (a combinator, a null value, an unspelled operator, the bare string or number) is what that door leaves as stored. Right.
- Step-18 rationale fragment (`migrations/registry.ts`, `STEP18_RATIONALE`, id `page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array`, order 36). Hand-written, outside the generated `semantic:18` region (the fragment sits at `:5024ff`; that region opens at `:5958`); only the inline clause is removed, id and order untouched; the sentence that remains is true. Right — and see ③ for the claim-line conflict.
- Changeset `.changeset/20305-inline-row-filter-converts.md`. Frontmatter `'@objectstack/spec': minor`; the title is true. Paragraph 1: the three inline shapes named are the three the removed function matched; "the binding's `dataSource.filter` included" is what the §1 pins assert. **Over-narrow, the one text defect:** "What still stays as stored, and is still reported as a TODO, is only a filter with a part that has no lossless rule spelling: a combinator, a null value, or an operator the rule vocabulary does not spell." The head clause is exact, but the enumeration after the colon reads as closed and omits three decline classes the code has — an array or object comparand in equality position, an empty operator object, and a rule the `ViewFilterRuleSchema` door refuses itself. Not false: the governing clause covers them, and the TODO row an operator reads names the real blocker; a CHANGELOG reader is under-told which TODOs remain. Paragraph 2: "match that filter against their own rows in objectui's in-memory data source (`ValueDataSource.find`)" true at the pin; "written against an objectui version whose `find` excluded every row for a rule array" true at `f8a9d0fb05`; "the same pin the previous release shipped" true by the tag reading; "114 filters on eight rows … null and missing values included" sourced to the dev report only (see above); "select no row on the objectui build just before that fix" true at `805abe240c`; "protecting nothing" follows. Operator bullets: `pending`, `skipped`, exit 1, `--apply` — each verified in `protocol.ts` and `meta.ts`; "every stored-row read replays the same rewrite" true (`stored.ts:104`); "shows the same rows" true at the pin. "Nothing an author writes is accepted or refused differently … no schema changes" true. The entries sentence is true. "ADR-0087 disposition: already registered" — the conversion and both D3 entries pre-date the merge base (registered in 17.5.0); a non-breaking changeset owes no marker, and `check:adr-0087-registration` is green. `Clause-②: no` present.
- PR body. Both sentences match the diff; `Clause-②: no` present. It does not name the pin flips, the registry regeneration or the changeset — an omission, not an error.
- Test header and comments. The §1 / §2 lines and the INLINE describe comment restate the pin reading above; "the fix's parent (no lowering) matched none" is right at `805abe240c`.

**Text left in place that the change bears on.** The `null` parenthetical — in the docblock ("the renderer skips that key today"), in the D3 entry ("the renderer skips that key, so it constrains nothing today, where a rule would test IS NULL") and in the runtime reason at `conversions/registry.ts:11230` ("the renderer skips a null-valued key, so today it constrains nothing … Drop the key") — is false for an inline-row block at the pin: `matchesFilter`'s scalar branch is `comparandEquals(value, condition)`, which is `===`, so `{ owner_id: null }` selects the rows whose `owner_id` is `null`, and dropping the key would widen that block. This PR does not create that: at `main` the filter's own blocker was read before the inline decline, so an inline node with a `null` value already received this very reason. What the PR does move is the D3 narrative, whose new "None of this depends on where a block's rows come from" now reads the parenthetical over inline blocks too, where it does not hold. The runtime string an operator acts on is unchanged by this diff; ruling 5893277767 grades the defect a separate card (③).

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `Clause-②: no` with no arm, in both the changeset and the PR body — well-formed under the closed pair, and consistent with the diff: no accept set moves (retired from the load path; no schema file; the §5 door pins), nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, no export goes, so this is not breaking and neither a `**BREAKING**` token nor an ADR-0087 marker is owed; the prose disposition names ids that pre-date the base. Not `skip-changeset`: the published conversion's reach over stored rows grows, and the stored pass's verdict flips for a class of databases (`skipped` / exit 0 to `pending` / exit 1), which a consumer observes. `patch` would be arguable (a stale guard removed) but `minor` is the safer level for a behaviour extension and matches the level the conversion itself shipped at in 17.5.0. The only other package whose observable behaviour moves is `@objectstack/cli`, through its dependency; its code is untouched and it takes the bump through the workspace, so no second changeset is owed. The over-narrow enumeration named in ① is a released-text imprecision and does not move the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 5893209491, on the live claim 5891237605 (its branch is the PR head branch; the "card this PR closes must claim this branch" check is green).

`open_questions` 1 — the `STEP18_RATIONALE` hunk, edited under the claim line "every text that describes the decline" against the line reading `migrations/registry.ts` as "regenerated only". Ruled A (keep) in 5893277767, and the ruling holds on the tree: the fragment is hand-written outside the generated markers, carries this conversion's own id, keeps id and order, and leaving the clause would have `os migrate meta` print a false sentence for the 17 to 18 hop; `packages/spec/scripts/step18-rationale-merge.test.ts` pins sort and order, both untouched. Answered.

`deviations` — (1) `Closes` for `Fixes`: both close the card; no action. (2) Labels and assignee not written by the dev: the fence's intent; the labels are on the PR now. (3) Container restart and resume, with `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt` re-run to exit 0 after the closure build: the head's check-runs answer every derived family, so nothing rides on the local record. (4) A first baseline run that selected no file and a first CLI run without dists: measurement hygiene, re-run correctly; CI is the record. (5) Worktrees removed: housekeeping. All answered.

`out_of_scope_findings` — (1) The `null` reason on inline-row blocks: verified at the pin as stated in ①; it pre-dates this PR; ruling 5893277767 escalates it to the seat's own card, whose number the inputs do not yet carry — the seat owes it, and the fix belongs to the null reason at `registry.ts:11230` and the D3 parenthetical, not to this diff. Escalated. (2) The pending changeset `20535-step18-rationale-fragments.md` ("byte-identical to the previous release"): verified overtaken before this PR — `92fe0814e0` (fragment order 47) and `542670da6d` (order 48) landed after `24d521e53e` introduced the fragments — so this PR does not newly falsify it; left to release-time notes compilation per the ruling. Answered.

Seat 2's earlier report 5890986192 (a blocked dispatch, no diff) raised the classifier denial and a claim-race reading; both are closed by release 5891011465 and the re-claim 5891237605, and its premise reading and surface inventory were carried over and re-measured here. Nothing open.

**Check-runs on the head** (read last; 46 runs, 35 distinct names after keeping the newest `started_at` per name; newest 2026-09-29T15:32Z): 30 `success`, 5 `skipped` (`Auto Label`, `Build Docs`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` — path filters and opt-ins; the diff removes no export the pinned sibling could import, so the pin gate has nothing to catch), 0 failures, none still running. `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates` (generated artifacts, pin citations, doc authoring, ADR-0087 registration), `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core` 1 to 6, the four `Type Check` jobs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the three claim checks are all green.
